title: Design an LLM API Gateway with Rate Limiting and Usage Metering
prompt: Design the API gateway that sits in front of an LLM product (like a chat-completions API): it authenticates requests, enforces per-customer rate limits and quotas, routes requests to the right model/backend, and meters token usage for billing.
requirements: Functional: authenticate API keys, enforce per-customer rate limits (requests/sec and tokens/min) and monthly quotas, route to the correct model backend, accurately meter token usage per request for billing

Non-functional: gateway must add minimal latency to every request, rate limiting must work correctly across many gateway instances, usage metering must not lose or double-count usage even under failures
discussion_points: Where rate-limit state lives so it's consistent across multiple gateway instances behind a load balancer
Rate limiting algorithm choice (token bucket, sliding window, etc.) and enforcing both a short-term rate and a longer-term quota
Metering streamed responses accurately (token counts often aren't known until the response finishes)
Ensuring billing usage records aren't lost or double-counted if a gateway instance crashes mid-request
Routing/load-balancing across multiple backend model deployments, including handling a backend that's overloaded or down
How a customer's quota gets reset periodically and how limit changes take effect without redeploying the gateway
